record.original_question: Given a positive integer n and prescribed numbers (p_α) indexed by all nonempty principal index sets α ∈ ⟨n⟩, does there exist an n × n matrix A whose principal minors satisfy A[α] = p_α for every nonempty α? More generally, how can this principal-minor assignment problem be solved or characterized for special matrix classes such as GKK, Hermitian, or nonnegative matrices?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let ⟨n⟩ = {1,2,…,n}. For an n×n matrix A over a field (e.g. ℝ or ℂ) and a nonempty subset α ⊆ ⟨n⟩, let A[α] denote the principal minor of A indexed by α, i.e. the determinant of the submatrix of A whose rows and columns are indexed by α. There are 2^n − 1 such nonempty principal minors.

Suppose that for every nonempty α ⊆ ⟨n⟩ a scalar p_α is prescribed. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the family (p_α)_{∅≠α⊆⟨n⟩} for the existence of an n×n matrix A satisfying

    A[α] = p_α   for every nonempty α ⊆ ⟨n⟩,

and, when such an A exists, describe how to construct it. Furthermore, address the same assignment problem within the following distinguished classes of matrices:
 (a) Hermitian matrices;
 (b) entrywise nonnegative matrices;
 (c) GKK τ-matrices (real matrices A all of whose principal minors are positive and which satisfy the property that for every principal submatrix B of A the spectrum of B lies in the open right half-plane and is symmetric with respect to the real axis).

Provide a characterization of the realizable families (p_α) in each case.
artifact.status_search_result: For general (non-symmetric) matrices over ℂ and ℝ, the principal minor assignment problem was studied by Griffin and Tsatsomeros (Principal minors, Parts I & II), giving a recursive constructive algorithm under genericity hypotheses. For symmetric/Hermitian matrices, Oeding (2011) proved the Holtz–Sturmfels conjecture set-theoretically: the variety of principal minors of n×n symmetric matrices is cut out by the orbit of Cayley's 2×2×2 hyperdeterminant under (SL₂)^n ⋊ S_n. Efficient algorithms for the symmetric case were given by Rising, Kulesza, and Taskar. For nonnegative matrices and especially for the GKK τ-matrix class, no complete characterization is known; the assignment problem in those classes remains open.

status_evidence.title: Principal minors, Part II: The principal minor assignment problem
status_evidence.snippet: The inverse problem of finding a matrix with prescribed principal minors is considered; a constructive recursive algorithm based on Schur complements is presented.
status_evidence.claim: The general PMAP has been studied with partial constructive solutions under genericity hypotheses.

status_evidence.title: Set-theoretic defining equations of the variety of principal minors of symmetric matrices
status_evidence.snippet: An irreducible G-module of degree 4 polynomials built from Cayley's 2×2×2 hyperdeterminant cuts out set-theoretically the variety of principal minors of n×n symmetric matrices, proving a conjecture of Holtz–Sturmfels.
status_evidence.claim: The symmetric case was resolved set-theoretically by Oeding.

status_evidence.title: An efficient algorithm for the symmetric principal minor assignment problem
status_evidence.snippet: An efficient algorithm is given for reconstructing a symmetric matrix from its principal minors when they are realizable.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithms exist for the symmetric/Hermitian case.
